messages.text:
Postmark: London postcards you can only make while standing at the landmark. One ticket: the core loop only.

The loop: ten London landmarks, each shown as a faded postcard with how far away you are. Inside 150 m the card unlocks and the live camera opens; no photos from the gallery, and the shutter works only inside the fence. The photo becomes the front of a postcard with a postmark stamp: landmark, date, time, coordinates, and "No. 3 of 10". Write one line on the back, then share it as an image through the phone's Share sheet (WhatsApp, Instagram), with "Collect your own at" and the page's link printed on the card. On desktop, download the image instead.

The first card is "Here": postmarked wherever you stand, so anyone outside London can try the whole loop.

Collected cards are kept on the phone (IndexedDB) and shown in a simple grid. Nothing is uploaded, no accounts.

Look: the app frame uses the house kit; the postcards themselves are warm and colourful, paper and ink, with a round postmark. System font stack for the frame, nothing loaded from the web except what the browser provides.

Landmarks (lat, lng): Tower Bridge 51.5055,-0.0754 · Elizabeth Tower 51.5007,-0.1246 · St Paul's Cathedral 51.5138,-0.0984 · Trafalgar Square 51.5080,-0.1281 · Buckingham Palace 51.5014,-0.1419 · London Eye 51.5033,-0.1196 · Tower of London 51.5081,-0.0759 · Piccadilly Circus 51.5101,-0.1340 · The Shard 51.5045,-0.0865 · Tate Modern 51.5076,-0.0994.

Green checks that need no browser: the fence logic in its own module, tested in node (inside 150 m unlocks, 151 m does not, for three landmarks); the postcard text block (landmark, date, time, coordinates, number) produced by a function, tested in node; no test or debug mode that bypasses the fence in the shipped page.

Out of scope: maps, accounts, minting, printing, sponsored stops, install to Home Screen, other cities.

Draft the brief.

Clear enough to build — with one push.

Ten illustrated postcards is ten pieces of art in one agent run. Make the card a single warm paper design with the landmark name set in type; the photo is the only image. That keeps the loop testable in minutes.

The "Here" card is worth keeping — it is what lets anyone outside London try the loop. The grid is a second feature; ship it as a plain list of saved cards and let the nice grid come later.

Nothing else changes. Say "ready" or press "Draft the brief" and the brief gets written against that.

brief.title: Postmark: London postcards that unlock only at the landmark
brief.task:
Write the project files first and improve them afterwards: index.html, style.css, fence.mjs, postcard.mjs, app.js and test.mjs, all dependency-free and opened straight from index.html. fence.mjs holds the ten named London landmarks with their lat/lng plus the "Here" card, a haversine distance function in metres, and an unlock function that is true at 150 m or less and false beyond it. postcard.mjs exports a function that takes a landmark name, a number, a date and coordinates and returns the printed postcard text block: landmark, date, time, coordinates to five decimals, and "No. N of 10". app.js shows the ten cards and the "Here" card faded with the distance in metres when geolocation is available, unlocks a card at 150 m or less and the "Here" card always, then opens a live getUserMedia camera with the rear facing — never a file or gallery picker — and the shutter stays disabled outside the fence. On capture, compose a PNG of the photo as the postcard front with one warm paper design, the landmark name set in type, and a round postmark stamp carrying landmark, date, time, coordinates, "No. N of 10" and the line "Collect your own at" with the page's own link; share it with navigator.share when file sharing is supported and download the image otherwise. Let the member write one line on the back, store the card in IndexedDB and list saved cards as a plain list of small thumbnails with name and date — no grid styling, no upload, no accounts. Load nothing from the network: system font stack for the frame, the house kit tokens only, no external fonts, scripts, images or CDNs. Do not install or audit any dependency, and ship no debug, bypass, skip-fence or unlock-all path in app.js — the fence lives only in fence.mjs and app.js calls it. test.mjs runs under plain node with no browser and asserts that 150 m unlocks and 151 m does not for three of the landmarks, and that the postcard text block for "No. 3 of 10" contains the landmark, date, time and coordinates.

Write files early; do not audit dependency source.
brief.goal: A phone web app where ten London landmarks and a universal "Here" card unlock inside 150 m, the live camera takes the shot, and the photo becomes a shareable postcard postmarked with place, date, time, coordinates and number.
out_of_scope: A styled grid of saved cards — a plain list is enough for this ticket
Ten illustrated card artworks — one warm paper card design with type-set names
Accounts, uploads, minting, printing or sponsored stops
Maps, other cities, Home Screen install
Any browser-based or manual end-to-end test harness

messages.text:
Upread Mini, first ticket: the reader only. PDFs, links, the shelf of past reads and suggested reads are later tickets, each its own build, because Upread v1 tried all of it at once and timed out.

Read any text on your phone one word at a time, at a speed you set. Two ways in: a built-in sample (the opening chapter of Darwin's On the Origin of Species, public domain) and a paste box for any text.

The reader: one word at a time in large type. Each word's anchor letter, about a third into the word as speed readers do, sits in one fixed slot about 35% from the left and is coloured. It must not move or jitter from word to word, sideways or up and down. Lay each word out around the slot: the letters before the anchor end exactly at the slot, the anchor is centred in it, the letters after start right after it. Never re-centre the whole word. Fixed font size and line height; wait for the font to load before reading. If a word still doesn't fit, shrink only that word's font until it does, with the anchor's centre unchanged. Green check: in a headless browser, over the first 200 words of the sample, the centre of the anchor letter stays within 1 px horizontally and vertically.

Speed slider from 150 to 900 words per minute, default 300. Tap to pause and play; when paused, show the sentence around the word. Pause slightly longer at commas and full stops. A thin progress bar and the time left.

Nothing is uploaded; no accounts. Out of scope for this ticket: PDFs, links, the shelf, install, sync, ads, games, AI summaries.

Draft the brief.

Clear enough to build. Two trims first.

Drop the web font wait. Use a system font stack. Nothing to load, no late swap to jitter the slot.

The headless-browser check needs a browser the builder cannot install alone in a few offline minutes. Instead, have the page measure itself: on load it lays out the sample's first 200 words, records each anchor centre, and prints the max off-slot distance on screen. The check reads that number.

Everything else stays as written. Say ready or press Draft the brief.

Ready, with one condition: the self-measure must lay out the words with the same reader code the user sees, read each anchor's position from the rendered element (getBoundingClientRect), and show the result at #check. No separate copy of the layout. Draft the brief.

**Brief: upread-mini — the reader only**

Product: upread-mini.

Title: Upread Mini: read text one word at a time.

Task: Build one static page. Embedded sample (the opening of Darwin's On the Origin of Species) and a paste box. The reader shows one word at a time in large type, on a system font stack, nothing fetched. The anchor letter's centre sits in a fixed slot about 35% from the left, coloured. Letters before the anchor end at the slot, the anchor is centred in it, letters after start right after it. The word is never re-centred. Fixed size and line height; a word that overflows shrinks its own font, anchor centre unchanged.

Slider 150 to 900 words per minute, default 300. Tap to pause and play; paused shows the surrounding sentence. Longer pause at commas and full stops. Thin progress bar and time left.

On load the page runs the first 200 words of the sample through the same layout code the reader uses, reads each anchor's centre with getBoundingClientRect, and prints the worst horizontal and vertical drift at #check.

Write the project files first, then improve them. Do not read or audit installed libraries. No dependencies, so no network checks needed beyond the page working offline.

Out of scope: PDFs, links, shelf, install, sync, ads, AI summaries.

brief.title: Upread Mini: read text one word at a time
brief.task:
Build a single static page, index.html, plus a small test script, test.mjs, and write both files first before refining them. The page carries an embedded sample (the opening of Darwin's On the Origin of Species, public domain) and a paste box, and reads out any text one word at a time in large type on a system font stack with nothing fetched from the network. Each word's anchor letter (about a third into the word) is coloured and its centre sits in a fixed slot about 35% from the left: letters before the anchor end exactly at the slot, letters after start right after it, and the whole word is never re-centred. Font size and line height are fixed; a word that would overflow shrinks only its own font until it fits, with the anchor's centre unchanged. A slider runs from 150 to 900 words per minute, default 300; tapping pauses and plays, and when paused the page shows the sentence around the current word; pauses are slightly longer at commas and full stops; a thin progress bar and the time left are shown. On load the page passes the sample's first 200 words through the same layout function the reader uses, reads each anchor centre with getBoundingClientRect, and prints the worst horizontal and vertical drift as a number at #check. test.mjs reads index.html as text and asserts it exits 0 when the page has the sample, the 150/900 slider bounds with a 300 default, the pause, progress and time-left elements, the #check element and getBoundingClientRect — it must not launch a browser or use the network. Do not read or audit the source or versions of any installed package; the page needs no dependencies. Out of scope for this ticket: PDFs, links, the shelf, install, sync, ads and AI summaries.

Write files early; do not audit dependency source.
